title: bug: release_task without force treats an explicit blank/null workerId as human and releases a live peer between steps
description:
Found during task-0adea941 QA repair self-review. The proxy injects only absent workerId keys; without force, releaseTask.ts reaches claimGuards.assertReleaseCaller's `if (!caller) return`, so explicit '' or null releases a peer-held row with no IN_PROGRESS step.
Snapshot /tmp/moe-0adea941-red-BP1LVK contains the repaired force gates plus a scratch '(follow-up)' test in src/tools/releaseForceGate.test.ts: npx vitest run src/tools/releaseForceGate.test.ts -t follow-up (env -i) passed 2 probes proving success:true and task-idle assignee null. Log: packages/nonforce-repro.log.
Keep this separate from the approved force-only contract: preserve genuine omitted-ID human/board recovery and legitimate own-row releases, refuse malformed supplied IDs before writes, and correct docs/MCP_SERVER.md:2030's stale 'Anyone can call — no ownership check' claim.
definitionOfDone: Without force, explicit blank/null/non-string caller IDs cannot release a peer-held row between steps and refusal writes nothing.
Absent-ID human/board recovery, valid own-row release, and governor/human force controls remain green.
release_task documentation accurately describes its ownership checks rather than saying there are none.
